newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fortis to pay max 12.7 bln bfr for ASLK-CGER stake.
newsitem.headline: Fortis to pay max 12.7 bln bfr for ASLK-CGER stake.

text.p: The Belgian Finance Ministry said on Wednesday the state's 9.8 percent stake in Belgian bank ASLK-CGER would be sold to Belgian-Dutch bankassurance group Fortis for a provisional 12.7 billion Belgian francs.

It said in a statement Fortis had reserved the right to refuse to buy the stake if the final price exceeded 12.7 billion francs. In that case the stake could be the subject of a private placement or a bourse listing.

The stake sale will raise Fortis' stake in ASLK to 60 percent and is part of an operation by the Belgian state to privatise a total 24.7 percent of ASLK. The 14.9 percent not going to Fortis are to be listed on the Brussels bourse.
The sale is the result of the Belgian government exercising a put option taken out at the time of the sale of an initial 49.9 percent in ASLK to Fortis in 1993.

The option was worth 6.8 billion francs at end-1993, rising to 8.5 billion at end-1997. Including "the substantialy improved profitability" of ASLK and the sharp rise in the general valuation of companies the agreed price was set at 12.7 billion.
"However, this price is subject to an adjustment mechanism linked to the possible flotation," the Finance Ministry said.

The 9.8 percent stake, held for the state by the Federal Participation Company, will be increased by 0.3 percent to 10.1 percent with Fortis exercising a call option on 0.1 percent and receiving 0.2 percent under a restructuring of ASLK.

The restructuring, a precursor to the flotation, will turn ASLK Insurance into a subsidiary of ASLK Bank, the entity which will be listed. As a result the "golden shares" which the two arms of the group held into each other to guarantee autonomous control will turned into ordinary shares and passed to Fortis.

Fortis said in a statement it would not need to borrow on the capital markets to finance the purchase since the financing of its recent acquisition of Dutch bank MeesPierson already took a possible extension of the stake in ASLK into account.
It said the acquisition at the agreed price would have a positive effect on earnings per share of Fortis AG and Fortis Amev, the Belgian and Dutch arms of the group.
